title: Enigma I instruction manual test message (Schlüsselanleitung zur Chiffriermaschine Enigma I)
plugboard: AM FI NV PS TU WZ
ciphertext: GCDSE AHUGW TQGRK VLFGX UCALX VYMIG MMNMF DXTGN VHVRM MEVOU YFZSL RHDRR XFJWC FHUHM UNZEF RDISI KBGPM YVXUZ
plaintext: FEIND LIQEI NFANT ERIEK OLONN EBEOB AQTET XANFA NGSUE DAUSG ANGBA ERWAL DEXEN DEDRE IKMOS TWAER TSNEU STADT
translation: Hostile column of infantry observed. Extends from the south exit of Bear Woods (Baerwalde) to position 3 km east of Neustadt. [German: Feindliche Infanteriekolonne beobachtet. Anfang Suedausgang Baerwalde. Ende 3 km ostwaerts Neustadt.]
excluded: Header '1035 - 90 - 341 -' (time, letter count, system indicator) and the first 6 letters 'PKPJX I' = the twice-enciphered message key (enciphered at Grundstellung FOL -> ABLABL). Full transmitted text as printed: PKPJX IGCDS EAHUG WTQGR KVLFG XUCAL XVYMI GMMNM FDXTG NVHVR MMEVO UYFZS LRHDR RXFJW CFHUH MUNZE FRDIS IKBGP MYVXU Z (96 letters).
caveats: Uses reflector UKW A (Weierud: machine 'rotors I, II, and III ... with the reflector, Umkehrwalze, A'); wiring of UKW A = EJMZALYXVBWFCRQUONTSPIKHGD (recovered by Marks & Weierud 1999). Pre-1938 procedure: message key enciphered twice at the fixed Grundstellung (given numerically as 06 15 12 = FOL). Header says 90 letters = the 90 body letters. Verified locally: PKPJXI at FOL -> ABLABL; body at ABL -> plaintext exactly as published.

title: Operation Barbarossa, SS-Totenkopf Division to LVI A.K., part 1 of 2
plugboard: AV BS CG DL FU HZ IN KM OW RX
ciphertext: EDPUD NRGYS ZRCXN UYTPO MRMBO FKTBZ REZKM LXLVE FGUEY SIOZV EQMIK UBPMM YLKLT TDEIS MDICA GYKUA CTCDO MOHWX MUUIA UBSTS LRNBZ SZWNR FXWFY SSXJZ VIJHI DISHP RKLKA YUPAD TXQSP INQMA TLPIF SVKDA SCTAC DPBOP VHJK
plaintext: AUFKL XABTE ILUNG XVONX KURTI NOWAX KURTI NOWAX NORDW ESTLX SEBEZ XSEBE ZXUAF FLIEG ERSTR ASZER IQTUN GXDUB ROWKI XDUBR OWKIX OPOTS CHKAX OPOTS CHKAX UMXEI NSAQT DREIN ULLXU HRANG ETRET ENXAN GRIFF XINFX RGTX
translation: Reconnaissance battalion from Kurtinowa north-west of Sebezh [on the] flight corridor towards Dubrowki, Opochka. Started to move at 18:30 hours. Attack. Inf[antry] R[e]g[imen]t ... (continues in part 2)
excluded: Header 'fuer m7g 1840 - 2tl 1tl 179 - WXC KCH -' (time 1840, 2 parts, this is part 1, 179 letters, Grundstellung WXC, enciphered message key KCH) and the first group RFUGZ, which is the Kenngruppe (unenciphered key-identification group, not part of the enciphered text).
caveats: Heer/Luftwaffe procedure in use from May 1940: operator-chosen Grundstellung sent in clear (WXC), message key enciphered once (KCH -> BLA). Letter count 179 = 5 (RFUGZ) + 174 body letters, so part 1 is complete. Franklin Heath prints the last group as 'VHJK-' (a 4-letter final group, not a missing letter). Key matches Weierud's 07.07.1941 key list (UKW B, W/O 245, Stecker AV BS CG DL FU HZ IN KM OW RX, Rings BUL). Verified locally: KCH at WXC -> BLA; body at BLA -> plaintext exactly as published (174 letters).

title: Scharnhorst's last message (Konteradmiral Bey), Duke of York intercept
plugboard: AN EZ HK IJ LR MQ OT PV SW UX
ciphertext: YKAE NZAP MSCH ZBFO CUVM RMDP YCOF HADZ IZME FXTH FLOL PZLF GGBO TGOX GRET DWTJ IQHL MXVJ WKZU ASTR
translation: Steering for Tanafjord. Position square AC 4992, speed 20 knots. Scharnhorst. [German: Steuere Tanafjord an. Standort Qu. AC 4992, Fahrt 20 sm. Scharnhorst]
excluded: Header 'Priority dots. 1925 21.' and the 4-letter indicator groups UTKZ RBSB (Schluesselkenngruppe + Verfahrenkenngruppe) at the start, which are repeated as the last two groups (UTKZ RBSB) at the end. Red-form transmission as printed: UTKZ RBSB YKAE ... ASTR UTKZ RBSB (24 groups).
caveats: Naval (Kenngruppenbuch) indicator procedure: Grundstellung is not published; the message key UZV is the recovered start position. The raw M4-Project break (bytereef) found an equivalent key with rings AGM / message key UYV and one wrong stecker (BJ instead of IJ) giving a partly garbled decrypt; the 'adjusted' key (rings AHM, UZV, stecker incl. IJ) gives the clean text used here. Header group count says 21 but 24 groups were received (Weierud). Plaintext 'HCO' at the end is unexplained padding. Verified locally: exact published plaintext (80 letters).

title: M4 Message Breaking Project, 1st break: Hartwig Looks, U-264 (HMS Hurricane intercept)
ringsFormat: number 1-26 (A=1); letters AAAV (greek wheel ring first)
plugboard: AT BL DF GJ HM NW OP QY RZ VX
translation: From Looks: radio signal 1132/19 contents: Forced to submerge during attack, depth charges. Last enemy location 08:30h, Marqu AJ 9863, 220 degrees, 8 knots, [I am] following. [Barometer 10]14 mb falling, NNO 4, visibility 10.
excluded: The bytereef source gives the ciphertext already 'stripped of indicator groups'; the original indicator/Kenngruppen groups from Erskine's Cryptologia letter are not included (not reproduced on the pages read).
caveats: Rings AAAV / key VJNA are the key as recovered by hill-climbing (an equivalent key; the historical ring settings of the left/greek wheels may differ, only effective offsets matter). Source prints W/O as 'B241' with 'UKW: B' — for M4 this means thin reflector B + greek wheel Beta + rotors II IV I. Plaintext contains operator garbles (e.g. 'SEYHS' for 'SECHS', 'EKNS' for 'EINS'). Verified locally: exact published plaintext (232 letters).

title: M4 Message Breaking Project, 2nd break: Hermann Schroeder, U-623 (HMS Hurricane intercept)
ringsFormat: number 1-26 (A=1); letters AANV (greek wheel ring first)
plugboard: AT CL DH EP FG IO JN KQ MU RX
translation: From Schroeder: Found nothing on convoy's course 55 degrees, moving to the ordered square. Position naval square AJ 3995. [Wind] SE 4, sea 3, 10/10 cloudy, [10]28 mb rising, fog, visibility 1 nautical mile.
excluded: Ciphertext as published is already 'stripped of indicator groups' (original indicator groups not included).
caveats: Date: message is 0246/21/203 (21 Nov 1942 per war-diary serial; the HMS Hurricane intercepts are dated 25 Nov 1942 on bytereef) — treat date as approximate. Rings AANV / key MCSF are the recovered (equivalent) key. Plaintext has garbles (SCHREEDER, MARSCAIERE, STANRORT, SEEDREM, NBBEL). Verified locally: exact published plaintext (200 letters).

title: M4 Project 'third message': Hermann Rasch, U-106 (HMS Hurricane intercept), broken 2013 by Dan Girard with Michael Hoerenberg
ringsFormat: number 1-26 (A=1); letters ZZDG (greek wheel ring first)
plugboard: BQ CR DI EJ KW MT OS PX UZ GH
translation: Boat clear. [Rendezvous] at Schnoor about 27 Nov. 60 cbm [fuel], provisions until 20 Dec. Need binoculars, only 4 serviceable. Am at naval square BB 25. Situation as Schaefer. [Wind] NW 5, 15 mb rising, good visibility. From Rasch.
excluded: Erskine's original intercept begins with indicator groups CLXP LWRU and ends with CDXP LWRU VA (as printed on hoerenberg 'Third Message'); these are excluded. Header 'T.O.R.1152/19/221 (53 GROUPS)'.
caveats: This is the DEGARBLED ciphertext used by Girard; it differs from Erskine's printed intercept at 6 positions (0-based index:orig>used): 16:U>C 32:H>R 66:C>O 129:X>K 130:C>O 186:?>X. Source lists 'Reflector: B' with 'Greek wheel: Beta' on an M4, i.e. thin B. Alternate equivalent key given by source: rings ZZTG, message key NBHL (also verified). Plaintext still contains garbles (GLMESER, VIEFKLHR, BRUNF, FUHF, ...). Date approximate (T.O.R. 1152/19). Verified locally: exact published raw plaintext (196 letters) with both keys.

title: Doenitz succession message recovered from U-534 (message P1030681), broken 2012 by Michael Hoerenberg
ringsFormat: number 1-26 (A=1); letters EPEL (greek wheel ring first)
plugboard: AE BF CM DQ HU JN LX PR SZ VW
indicator: DUHF TETO (-> Verfahrenkenngruppe QEOB via Doppelbuchstabentauschtafel; QEOB at Grundstellung NAEM -> CDSZ)
ciphertext: LANO TCTO UARB BFPM HPHG CZXT DYGA HGUF XGEW KBLK GJWL QXXT GPJJ AVTO CKZF SLPP QIHZ FXOE BWII EKFZ LCLO AQJU LJOY HSSM BBGW HZAN VOII PYRB RTDJ QDJJ OQKC XWDN BBTY VXLY TAPG VEAT XSON PNYN QFUD BBHH VWEP YEYD OHNL XKZD NWRH DUWU JUMW WVII WZXI VIUQ DRHY MNCY EFUA PNHO TKHK GDNP SAKN UAGH JZSM JBMH VTRE QEDG XHLZ WIFU SKDQ VELN MIMI THBH DBWV HDFY HJOQ IHOR TDJD BWXE MEAY XGYQ XOHF DMYU XXNO JAZR SGHP LWML RECW WUTL RTTV LBHY OORG LGOW UXNX HMHY FAAC QEKT HSJW
translation: War emergency message to all: The following is to be announced immediately: I have received the following order: 'In place of former Reichsmarschall Goering the Fuehrer has appointed you, Herr Grossadmiral, as his successor. Written authorization on the way. Effective immediately you are to order all measures required by the present situation.' Signed Reichsleiter (Tulpe) Bormann. [From] C-in-C Navy, via radio station of the Commanding Admiral U-boats.
excluded: Indicator groups DUHF TETO at the start and their repetition DUHF TETO at the end (cryptomuseum: 'should be ignored as they are not part of the text').
caveats: This is NOT one of the 2006 M4-Project messages; it is one of the U-534 messages broken by Hoerenberg (2012). The cryptomuseum settings table gives Grundstellung NAEM, but its prose says 'at the basic setting (Grundstellung) NEAM' — NEAM is a typo: verified locally QEOB at NAEM -> CDSZ, at NEAM -> LYHC. Reflector on M4 is thin C combined with Beta (unusual; normally C-thin with Gamma). The ciphertext is a reconstruction from two garbled copies (Dan Girard, 'Degarbling the Doenitz Message'); the plaintext still contains garbles (FOLGELNBE, ANSTERLE, BISHERIGXN, HVRR GRZSSADMIRAL, SCHRIFTLSCHE, REICHSLEITEI). Wikipedia's worked example (window positions CDTK... for plaintext letter F at ciphertext 'RBBF...') is consistent with CDSZ at 'LANO'. Verified locally: exact published plaintext (372 letters).

title: Heeresgruppe Nord (Barbarossa) short message Nr. 113 (XIVFG), same 07.07.1941 daily key
plugboard: AV BS CG DL FU HZ IN KM OW RX
ciphertext: IBAVL EQQLT IUMMJ REOCI IYYVO A
translation: Where is the numbers report? Query. (own translation)
excluded: Header '1245 - 31 - LMN JGO -' and Kenngruppe XIVFG (first group). 31 letters = 5 + 26 body.
caveats: PLAINTEXT NOT PUBLISHED on the pages read: Weierud lists the message as 'Broken' and gives the key (key list: Kenngruppe XIVFG, Indicator LMN JGO, Start OPQ, Stop OQQ) but no printed plaintext was found; the plaintext here is a decryption with the published key (clean German, so key/ciphertext are almost certainly right). Useful as a short (26-letter) hard case. Verified: JGO at LMN -> OPQ.
